SMTO-JOB-0016 — The Gateway couldn't start this background job

GUID: 1c537bb1-4b53-4acc-8554-88db03198aac
Slug: gateway-job-runtime-unavailable
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • The Gateway (the helper program that runs commands on a computer) couldn't take on this background job because its job service isn't working right now. The job did not start, so nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway that should run the job. This shows whether SMTO can reach that Gateway and whether it reports a problem.
  2. When no other tasks are running on that computer, restart the Gateway there. For the LocalMachine Gateway, restart SMTO itself. Restarting brings the job service back up, and waiting first avoids stopping other work.
  3. If it still fails, ask the person who manages that computer to check for a Gateway update in Settings › Setup › Gateways or run the Gateway installer again. A damaged or incomplete installation can keep the job service from starting.
  4. Once Check connection succeeds, ask the agent to start the job again. This job never started, so starting it again won't repeat any work.

What success looks like

  • Check connection succeeds for the Gateway and the job shows as running.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete the Gateway's data folder or turn off its security checks to get it working.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway returned a definite non-admission (gateway_job_runtime_unavailable): its job runtime or worker admission failed before any dispatch record existed, so the job was not started.

What this means

  • The job runtime returns a definite non-admission result, including an IPC admission failure before any durable dispatch fence exists. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • The job runtime returns a definite non-admission result, including an IPC admission failure before any durable dispatch fence exists.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect job-runtime readiness, owner/fence/storage admission diagnostics; this kind does not itself prove missing installation packages.

How to fix it

  • Check the Gateway log on that node for the job-runtime or IPC admission failure, confirm the Gateway installation is complete and current (rerun the supported Gateway installer only if files are missing or damaged), then restart the Gateway once active work has settled. Do not remove the Gateway's saved state or weaken its trust checks to make it look healthy.
  • Resolve the specific Gateway runtime/admission failure; repair installation only when indicated, and restart through supported controls after active work settles.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual runtime admission problem is resolved and job readiness passes before new launch work.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-GWT-0026 — Gateway job control unavailable
  • SMTO-JOB-0001 — SMTO can't tell whether a background job ran
